notes: inherent: The inherent vowel is typed 'o' or 'a' (কর kor, বল bol, কলকাতা kolkata / kalkata); at the end of a word it is mostly dropped (আমার amar), but kept after a final cluster (গল্প golpo) and often where it is said (ভাল bhalo). In the middle of a word it is dropped between a vowel + lone consonant and a lone consonant + vowel (রাজনীতি rajniti, কলকাতা kolkata). phalas: The -ya sign after a consonant is 'y' or nothing (ব্যাপার byapar / bapar, সন্ধ্যা sondhya / sondha), the -ba sign mostly nothing or 'w' (স্বাধীন swadhin / shadhin, বিশ্ব bishwo), and ম after a virama is usually 'm' (আত্মা atma). Speech doubles the consonant instead, and chat spells what is said (অন্য onno, ধন্যবাদ dhonnobad, সত্য sotto, বিশ্ব bissho, পদ্ম poddo), so the common consonant + -ya, -ba and -ma pairs are listed in clusters with the doubled spelling as an option. The doubled spelling has another skeleton than the y or w one, so those forms reach their word through the transliterator, which learns them from these tables. ম্ব, ল্ব and ব্ব keep their b. letters: অ্যা (অ + -ya sign + আ-kar, also written এ্যা) is the a of English loans (অ্যাপ app, অ্যান্ড and) and is one key of four code points. র (U+09B0) is r; the Assamese ৰ and ৱ are not Bengali letters and are not in the tables. য is j (যদি jodi) and য় is y (হয় hoy, মেয়ে meye). য় ড় ঢ় are base + nukta after NFC (U+09DF etc. are composition exclusions), so their keys are two code points. ড় is r only (বাড়ি bari, বড় boro): Aksharantar's annotators mostly typed d, a transliteration habit that chat does not have, and with d listed the fit would key every such word by d. ৎ, ং, ঁ and ঃ are finals. স is said sh and typed s or sh (সব sob / shob). skeleton: sh folds to s and chh, ch to c; z to j; v and w to b; f to p; o to a, so the inherent vowel typed o or a gives one key (বল bol / bal); y to i (হয় hoy / hoi). kkh, ksh and khy fold to k (ক্ষমা khoma / kshoma). gy folds to g (জ্ঞান gyan / ggan), wri to ri (বৃষ্টি bwrishti / brishti), ng before k or s to n (ব্যাংক byangk / bank), mb and mp to nb and np. An a between two consonants is dropped, so the inherent vowel that speech drops gives one key typed or not (আমরা amara / amra, করব korobo / korbo); with o and aa folded to a this also drops a typed o or aa there, so the letters between consonants are told apart only by ranking. A final a after a consonant is dropped, which covers the final inherent vowel typed or not (ভাল bhal / bhalo).
